en: Having or showing ambition; wanting a lot of power, honor, respect, superiority, or other distinction.
Very desirous.

ambitious.ety: From Middle English ambitious, from Middle French ambitieus, from Latin ambitiosus, from ambitio; see ambition. Compare with French ambitieux. By surface analysis, ambit + -ious.

ex.en: His next production was a very ambitious musical.
ex.ja: 彼の次の制作は非常に意欲的なミュージカルだった。

ex.en: They say that he was ambitious when young.
ex.ja: 彼は若いころ野心家だったそうだ。

ex.en: He was ambitious of success in business.
ex.ja: 彼は実業家として成功したいと熱望していた。

note.ja: ambition（野心）+ -ous。ラテン語 ambitio ＝ amb（周りを）+ ire（行く）。「票を求めて歩き回ること」→「野心」。

en: In the middle of; in the center of; surrounded by.

amid.ety: From Middle English amidde, Old English onmiddan, on middan, a- + mid.

ex.en: She was standing amid the ruins of the castle.
ex.ja: 彼女は城の廃墟の中にたたずんでいた。

ex.en: The tower stood amid the ruins.
ex.ja: その塔は廃墟の中に立っていた。

ex.en: They are amid the city noises.
ex.ja: 彼らは町の騒音の真っただ中にいる。

note.ja: amidst の短縮。a（〜に）+ mid（真ん中）。「〜の真っただ中で」。

en: Troubled, irritated by something unwanted or unliked (an annoyance); vexed.

ex.en: I get annoyed when I am kept waiting.
ex.ja: 待たされている時はいつもいらいらする。

ex.en: I was annoyed that she was still asleep.
ex.ja: 彼女がまだ寝ているのには頭にきた。

ex.en: Don't bother getting annoyed over something like that.
ex.ja: そんなことでイライラすんなよ。

note.ja: annoy（いらいらさせる）+ -ed。ラテン語 in odio（憎しみの中に）から。odious（憎らしい）と同じ。

en: A classical form of dance.
A theatrical presentation of such dancing, usually with music, sometimes in the form of a story.
To perform an action reminiscent of ballet dancing.

Borrowed from French ballet, from Italian balletto (“short dance, ballet”), diminutive form of ballo (“group dance”) (cognate with Old French bal, whence English ball), from Late Latin ballō (“to dance”).

ex.en: I consider the Russian ballet the greatest.
ex.ja: 私はロシアのバレエが一番素晴らしいと思います。

ex.en: She invited me to the ballet.
ex.ja: 彼女は私をバレエに招待してくれた。

ex.en: I don't know anything about ballet.
ex.ja: バレエのことはとんと分からない。

note.ja: イタリア語 balletto（小さな踊り）から。ballo（踊り）+ 縮小。ball（舞踏会）と同じ。

en: An agreement between parties concerning the sale of property; or a contract by which one party binds themself to transfer the right to so…
An agreement or stipulation; mutual pledge.
To make a bargain; to make a deal or contract for the exchange of property or services; to negotiate; to haggle.
To transfer for a consideration; to barter; to trade

bargain.ety:
From Middle English bargaynen (“to bargain, make a pledge for sale”), from Old French bargaigner (“to bargain”), from Frankish *borganjan (“to borrow, lend”), from Proto-Germanic *burgijaną (“to borrow, lend”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰergʰ- (“to protect, secure”). Akin to Old High German boragēn, borgēn (“to look after, care for”) (German borgen), Old English borgian (“to borrow, lend, pledge”). More at borrow.
Compare French barguigner and Portuguese barganhar.

ex.en: She has an eye on a good bargain.
ex.ja: 彼女はバーゲンには抜け目がない。

ex.en: I got this TV at a bargain price.
ex.ja: このテレビはバーゲンで買ったんだ。

ex.en: I bought this TV set at a bargain sale.
ex.ja: このテレビはバーゲンで買ったんだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 bargaignier（値切る）から。「値段を交渉する」→「取引・お買い得品」。

en: Being in one of two mutually exclusive states.
Concerning logic whose subject matter concerns such states.
A state in which only two values are possible, in which something must have one value or the other.
The bijective base-2 numeral system, which uses only the digits 0 and 1.

ex.en: Tom is non-binary.
ex.ja: トムはXジェンダーですよ。

en: A mixture of two or more things.
A word formed by combining two other words; a portmanteau word.
To mingle; to mix; to unite intimately; to pass or shade insensibly into each other.
To be mingled or mixed.

blend.ety: From Middle English blenden, either from Old English blandan, blondan, ġeblandan, ġeblendan or from Old Norse blanda (“to blend, mix”) (which was originally a strong verb with the present-tense stem blend; compare blendingr (“a blending, a mixture; a half-breed”)), whence also Danish blande, or from a blend of the Old English and Old Norse terms; both ultimately from Proto-Germanic *blandaną (“to blend; mix; combine”). Compare Middle Dutch blanden (“to mix”), Gothic 𐌱𐌻𐌰𐌽𐌳𐌰𐌽 (blandan), Old Church Slavonic блєсти (blesti, “to go astray”).

ex.en: The sky seemed to blend with the sea.
ex.ja: 空が海と一つに溶け込むように見えた。

ex.en: Blend the blue paint with the yellow paint.
ex.ja: 青い絵の具と黄色の絵の具を混ぜなさい。

ex.en: Blend the red paint with the blue paint.
ex.ja: 赤い絵の具に青い絵の具を混ぜなさい。

note.ja: 北欧語 blanda（混ぜる）から。「混ぜる・溶け込む」。

en: A man in business, one who works at a commercial institution.

businessman.ety: From business + -man. Displaced earlier merchant, ultimately from Latin mercāns (“merchant, buyer”).

ex.en: As a businessman he is far above me.
ex.ja: 実業家として彼は私よりはるかに優れている。

ex.en: He has a good record as a businessman.
ex.ja: 彼は実業家として良い実績をあげている。

ex.en: A good businessman knows how to make money.
ex.ja: 良いビジネスマンは金の儲けかたを知っている。

note.ja: business（仕事）+ man。business は busy（忙しい）+ ness。

en: An instance of colliding.
Any event in which two or more bodies exert forces on each other in a relatively short time. In a collision, physical contact of two bodi…

collision.ety: From Middle French collision, from Latin collīsiō (“clash, concussion, collision”) (whence -ion (noun suffix denoting action, result, process, state, condition)), from collīsus (“clashed together, conflicted, contended”), past participle of collīdō (“to clash, strike, dash, beat, or press together”) (whence collide), from con- (“together”) + laedō (“to strike, collide, hurt”) (whence col- (assimilated form of com-)).

ex.en: There was a multiple collision on the highway.
ex.ja: 高速道路では多数の衝突があった。

ex.en: It was a head-on collision.
ex.ja: 正面衝突だった。

ex.en: His story of the collision agrees with mine.
ex.ja: その衝突について彼が言う事はぼくのと一致する。

note.ja: col（共に）+ laedere（打つ）+ -ion。「互いにぶつかること」→「衝突」。collide。

en: Deep awareness of the suffering of others that people have to the point of them being motivated to relieve such states.
Deep awareness of the individual experiences of suffering of others or themselves that people have to the point of them being motivated t…

compassion.ety: From Middle English compassioun, compassion, from Old French compassion, from Ecclesiastical Latin compassio (“sympathy”), from Latin compati, past participle compassus (“to suffer together with”), from com- (“together”) + pati (“to suffer”); see passion. By surface analysis, com- + passion.

ex.en: Nothing is as important as compassion.
ex.ja: 同情ほどたいせつなものはない。

ex.en: Try to have some compassion.
ex.ja: 慈悲の心を持ってごらん。

ex.en: Compassion is entirely absent from his character.
ex.ja: 彼の性格には同情心がまったく欠けている。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pass（苦しむ）+ ion。共に苦しむこと →「思いやり・同情」。sympathy（共に感じる）と同じ発想。

ex.en: The whole village was consumed by the fire.
ex.ja: 全村が火事で焼けてなくなった。

ex.en: Role-playing video games are time consuming.
ex.ja: ロールプレイングのテレビゲームは時間を食う。

ex.en: The car consumes a lot of fuel.
ex.ja: その車は多量の燃料を消費する。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ sum（取る）+ e。すっかり取り尽くす →「消費する・食べ尽くす」。

en: The act of correcting.
A substitution for an error or mistake.

correction.ety: From Middle English correccioun, correction, from Old French correccion (French correction), from Latin corrēctiō. Doublet of correctio.

ex.en: Thank you for the corrections.
ex.ja: 添削していただいてありがとうございました。

ex.en: I welcome any corrections or additions to these minutes.
ex.ja: この議事録に関して、訂正、追加がありましたらお願いします。

ex.en: He made several corrections.
ex.ja: 彼はいくつか訂正をした。

note.ja: cor（完全に）+ rect（まっすぐ）+ ion。まっすぐに直すこと →「訂正・修正」。

en: Sometimes followed by up: to force (something) out of the lungs or throat by pushing air from the lungs through the glottis (causing a sh…
To cause (oneself or something) to be in a certain condition in the manner described in etymology 1 sense 1.1.
A sudden, often involuntary expulsion of air from the lungs through the glottis (causing a short, explosive sound), and out through the m…
A bout of repeated coughing (verb etymology 1 sense 2.1); also, a medical condition that causes one to cough.
Used to represent the sound of a cough (noun sense 1), especially when focusing attention on a following utterance, often an attribution …

cough.ety:
From Middle English coughen, coghen (“to cough; to vomit”) [and other forms], from Old English *cohhian (compare Old English cohhetan (“to bluster; to riot; to cough (?)”)), from Proto-West Germanic *kuh- (“to cough”), ultimately of onomatopoeic origin.
Cognates
* Middle Dutch cuchen (“to cough”) (modern Dutch kuchen (“to cough”); German Low German kuchen (“to cough”))
* Middle High German kûchen (“to breathe (on); to exhale”), kîchen (“to breathe with difficulty”) (modern German keichen, keuchen (“to breathe with difficulty; to gasp, pant”))
* Spanish cof (“coughing sound”)
* West Frisian kic

ex.en: Jimmy is coughing badly because he has a cold.
ex.ja: ジミーはかぜをひいているので、ひどいせきをしている。

ex.en: I cannot get rid of my cough.
ex.ja: どうしても咳がとれないの。

ex.en: I couldn't sleep last night. I coughed a lot.
ex.ja: 昨夜は、咳き込んで眠れなかった。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。せきの「ゴホッ」という音から。gh は［f］と発音する。

en: Of, from, or pertaining to Czechia, the Czech people, culture, or language.
A person from the Czech Republic (Czechia) or of Czech descent.

Czech.ety: Unadapted borrowing from Polish Czech, from Old Polish Czech, from Old Czech Čech, ultimately a variation and contraction of Proto-Slavic *čelověkъ (“human”).

ex.en: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic.
ex.ja: プラハはチェコ共和国の首都だ。

note.ja: チェコ語 Čech（チェコ人）から。

en: A storage facility, in particular, a warehouse.
A storage space for public transport and other vehicles where they can be maintained and from which they are dispatched for service.

depot.ety: From French dépôt, from Old French depost, from Medieval Latin dēpositum, from Latin, participle of dēpōnō, dēpōnere. Doublet of deposit.

ex.en: The buses return to the depot at night.
ex.ja: バスは夜になると車庫に戻る。

note.ja: フランス語 dépôt（預けた所）から。de（下に）+ ponere（置く）。「物を置いておく所」→「倉庫・発着所」。deposit と同じ。

en: Physical or emotional discomfort, suffering, or alarm, particularly of a more acute nature.
A cause of such discomfort.
To cause strain or anxiety to someone.
To retain someone’s property against the payment of a debt; to distrain.

distress.ety:
The verb is from Middle English distressen, from Old French destrecier (“to restrain, constrain, put in straits, afflict, distress”); compare French détresse. Ultimately from Medieval Latin as if *districtiō, an assumed frequentative form of Latin distringō (“to pull asunder, stretch out”), from dis- (“apart”) + stringō (“to draw tight, strain”).
The noun is from Middle English distresse, from Old French destrece, ultimately also from Latin distringō.

ex.en: Her death was a great distress to all the family.
ex.ja: 彼女の死で家族全員が悲嘆に暮れた。

ex.en: Famine caused great distress among the people.
ex.ja: 飢饉が人々にひどい窮乏をもたらした。

ex.en: Many people were plunged into distress by the news.
ex.ja: その知らせは多くの人々を苦悩におとしいれた。

note.ja: dis（離して）+ stringere（きつく締める）。「ぎゅっと締めつける」→「苦痛・困窮」。stress、strict と同じ。

en: A documentary.

documentation.ety: From document + -ation or Medieval Latin documentātio.

ex.en: Please read the documentation before you install the software.
ex.ja: ソフトウェアをインストールする前に説明書を読んでください。

note.ja: document（文書）+ -ation。ラテン語 docere（教える）から。「教えるための資料」→「文書」。doctor と同じ doc。

ex.ja: 日経指数は大引け間際に大きく跳ね上がりました。

en: Characterised by or exhibiting elegance; having grace, refinement, or tasteful simplicity.
Characterised by minimalism and intuitiveness while preserving exactness and precision.
An elegant parrot.

elegant.ety: From Late Middle English elegaunt, from Middle French elegant, ultimately from Latin ēlegāns, collateral form of present participle of ēligere, from ex- (“out of, from”) + legō (“choose, select, appoint”).

ex.en: She has an elegant manner.
ex.ja: 彼女は上品な態度をしています。

ex.en: She looks very elegant.
ex.ja: 彼女はとても優雅に見える。

ex.en: He fashioned an elegant pot out of clay.
ex.ja: 彼は、粘土で優雅な壷を形作った。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ leg（選ぶ）+ ant。（多くの中から）選び抜かれた →「優雅な・洗練された」。

ex.en: We went up and down in the elevator.
ex.ja: 私たちはエレベーターで上がったり下がったりした。

en: A holiday, festival, especially a religious one
A very large meal, often of a ceremonial nature.
To partake in a feast, or large meal.
To dwell upon (something) with delight.

feast.ety: From Middle English feeste, feste, borrowed from Old French feste, from Late Latin festa, from the plural of Latin festum (“holiday, festival, feast”), from Proto-Italic *fēs-tos, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéh₁s (“god, godhead, deity”); see also Ancient Greek θεός (theós, “god, goddess”). More at theo-. Doublet of fete, fiesta, and fest. Displaced Old English wīnhāte.

ex.en: He made a speech at the wedding feast.
ex.ja: 彼は結婚披露宴でスピーチをした。

ex.en: Her lovely voice was a real feast to the ears.
ex.ja: 彼女の美しい声は耳にとても心地よく響いた。

ex.en: My work is always feast or famine.
ex.ja: 私の仕事はいつも多すぎるか少なすぎるかのどちらかである。

note.ja: ラテン語 festa（祭り）から。festival と同じ。「祭り」→「祝宴・ごちそう」。

The cold weather that causes these ice crystals to form.
To cover with frost.
To become covered with frost.

ex.en: The plants were damaged by the late frost.
ex.ja: その植物は遅霜で被害を受けた。

ex.en: The ground was covered with frost this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝、地面は霜で覆われていた。

ex.en: The plants were damaged by the frost.
ex.ja: その植物は霜で被害を受けた。

en: A messenger, especially one bringing important news.
A harbinger, giving signs of things to come.
To proclaim or announce an event.
To greet something with excitement; to hail.

herald.ety: From Latin heraldus, from Middle English herald, herauld, heraud, from Anglo-Norman heraud, from Old French heraut, hiraut (modern French héraut), from Frankish *heriwald, from Proto-Germanic *harjawaldaz, a compound consisting of Proto-Indo-European *ker- (“army”) + *h₂welh₁- (“to be strong”). Doublet of Harold and Harald; compare Walter, which has these elements reversed.

ex.en: The first flowers herald the arrival of spring.
ex.ja: 最初の花が春の訪れを告げる。

note.ja: 古フランス語 heraut（布告役人）から。ゲルマン系で「軍の役人」。→「先触れ・告げる」。

en: A long walk, usually for pleasure or exercise.
An abrupt increase.
To take a long walk (on something) for pleasure or exercise.
To unfairly or suddenly raise a price.
Let's go; get moving. A command to a dog sled team, given by a musher.

hike.ety: From English dialectal hyke (“to walk vigorously”), probably a Northern form of hitch, from Middle English hytchen, hichen, icchen (“to move, jerk, stir”). Cognate with Scots hyke (“to move with a jerk”), dialectal German hicken (“to hobble, walk with a limp”), Danish hinke (“to hop”).

ex.en: Not really. I like hiking better than fishing.
ex.ja: 遠慮しておきます。釣りよりハイキングのほうが好きなんです。

ex.en: We are to go on a hike tomorrow.
ex.ja: ぼくたちは明日ハイキングに行く予定なんだ。

ex.en: Bring a lunch for our day of hiking.
ex.ja: ハイキングの日にランチを持ってきなさい。

note.ja: 語源は不詳。19世紀ごろから「歩き回る」→「ハイキング」、ぐいと引き上げる →「（価格の）引き上げ」。

en: A small valley between mountains.
A sunken area on a surface.
to make a hole in something; to excavate
Having an empty space or cavity inside.
Distant, eerie; echoing, reverberating, as if in a hollow space; dull, muffled; often low-pitched.
Completely, as part of the phrase beat hollow or beat all hollow.

hollow.ety: From Middle English holow, holowe, holwe, holwȝ, holgh, from Old English holh (“a hollow”), from Proto-West Germanic *holh, from Proto-Germanic *hulwiją, from Proto-Germanic *hulaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to cover, hide”). Cognate with Old High German huliwa and hulwa, Middle High German hülwe. Related to hole.

ex.en: My life is hollow without him.
ex.ja: 彼のいない人生はむなしい。

ex.en: The fox hid in the hollow tree.
ex.ja: キツネは穴があいた木の中へ隠れた。

ex.en: I saw a woman with hollow cheeks.
ex.ja: 私はほほのこけた女性にあった。

note.ja: 古英語 holh（穴）から。hole（穴）と同じ。「穴のある」→「空洞の・うつろな」。

en: The country that one regards as home.
One's country of residence.

ex.en: He was never to see his homeland again.
ex.ja: 彼はその後再び故国を見ることはなかった。

ex.en: They abandoned their homeland.
ex.ja: 彼らは故国を捨てた。

ex.en: The soldiers ached for their homeland.
ex.ja: 兵士たちは故国が恋しくてならなかった。

note.ja: home（家・故郷）+ land（土地）。「生まれ育った土地」→「祖国」。

en: In an international manner.

internationally.ety:
Etymology tree
English international
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English internationally
From international + -ly.

ex.en: We are internationally competitive in production technology.
ex.ja: 私たちは生産技術では国際的に競争力がある。

ex.en: Kyoto is internationally famous for its scenic beauty.
ex.ja: 京都は景色が美しい点で国際的にも有名です。

note.ja: inter（間）+ nation（国）+ -al + -ly。「国と国の間で」→「国際的に」。

en: Of, from, or pertaining to Iraq, or the Iraqi people.
Of, from, or pertaining to Persian Iraq.
A person from Iraq or of Iraqi descent.

Iraqi.ety: Borrowed from Arabic عِرَاقِيّ (ʕirāqiyy, “Iraqi”), equivalent to Iraq + -i.

ex.en: The Iraqi team won the football match.
ex.ja: イラクのチームがサッカーの試合に勝った。

note.ja: Iraq + -i（〜の人・〜の）。Pakistani と同じ作り。

en: Unable to walk properly because of a problem with one's feet or legs.
That cannot be moved properly.
To cause (a person or animal) to become lame.
A thin layer or plate of material, as in certain kinds of armor.
A set of joined overlapping metal plates.

lame.ety: From Middle English lame, from Old English lama (“lame”), from Proto-West Germanic *lam, from Proto-Germanic *lamaz (“lame”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃lemH- (“to tire; to break”).

ex.en: I don't want to be lame; I want to be cool!!
ex.ja: ダサい奴には、なりたくない。かっこよくなりたい！

ex.en: Now the President is nothing but a lame duck.
ex.ja: 今や大統領はレイム・ダックにすぎません。

note.ja: 古英語 lama（体が不自由な）から。→「説得力のない」→ 俗に「ださい」。

en: Any of several flowers in the genus Lilium of the family Liliaceae, which includes a great many ornamental species.
Any of several species of herbaceous flower which may or may not resemble the genus Lilium in some way, and which are not closely related…

lily.ety: From Middle English lilie, from Old English lilie, from Latin līlia, plural of līlium, from Ancient Greek λείριον (leírion). See there for more.

ex.en: This flower is called a lily in English.
ex.ja: この花は英語でｌｉｌｙと呼ばれる。

ex.en: A smell of lilies filled the room.
ex.ja: ユリの香りが部屋に満ちていた。

ex.en: A white lily is very beautiful to look at.
ex.ja: 白いゆりは見た目がとてもきれいだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 lilium から。ギリシャ語 leirion。

en: A type of storage compartment with a lock, usually used to store personal possessions for public use, such as in schools, railway station…
A lockable cubicle.

locker.ety: From lock + -er (patient suffix) or -er (agent noun suffix). Related to German Loch, Dutch luik, and Dutch loket.

ex.en: Each of the students has his own locker.
ex.ja: 学生たちはめいめい個人用のロッカーがある。

ex.en: While swimming in the pool, she lost her locker key.
ex.ja: プールで泳いでいる間に、彼女はロッカーの鍵をなくした。

ex.en: Each student has their own locker.
ex.ja: 学生たちはめいめい個人用のロッカーがある。

note.ja: lock（錠）+ -er。「鍵をかける戸棚」→「ロッカー」。

en: The continent; the principal land, as distinguished from islands or a peninsula.
The principal island of a group.

mainland.ety: From Middle English mayne londe; equivalent to main + land. Compare Scots mayn-land, magan-land, madin-land (“mainland”), Faroese meginland (“mainland”), Icelandic meginland (“mainland”).

ex.en: The island is cut off far from the mainland.
ex.ja: その島は本土から遠く離れている。

ex.en: We took a ferry from the island to the mainland.
ex.ja: 我々は島から本土へフェリーで渡った。

ex.en: All communication with the mainland was cut off by the typhoon.
ex.ja: 台風で本土との通信が絶えた。

note.ja: main（主な）+ land（陸）。「主な陸地」→「本土」。

en: A devotional exercise of, or leading to, contemplation.
Any of various types of achieving more or less altered states of consciousness, such as vacancy of mind or prolonged contemplation on a s…

meditation.ety: From Old French meditacion, from Latin meditatio, from meditatus, the past participle of meditārī (“to meditate, to think over, consider”), itself from Proto-Indo-European *med- (“to measure, limit, consider, advise”).

ex.en: He hit on the plan after long meditation.
ex.ja: 彼は長い間熟考した後、その計画を思いついた。

ex.en: A sudden loud noise broke in on my meditation.
ex.ja: 外で突然大きな物音がして私の瞑想は中断した。

ex.en: He painted an image he had during meditation last night.
ex.ja: 彼は昨晩瞑想した時のイメージを描いた。

note.ja: meditate（瞑想する）+ -ation。ラテン語 meditari（考える）、mederi（手当てする）と同系で、medicine と遠い親戚とされる。

en: One who brings messages.
The secretary bird.
To send something by messenger.

messenger.ety:
From Middle English messengere, messingere, messangere, from Old French messanger, a variant of Old French messagier (French messager), equivalent to message + -er. Doublet of messager.
Displaced native Old English boda (“messenger, envoy”) and ǣrendraca (“messenger, ambassador”).
For the replacement of -ager with -enger, -inger, -anger, compare passenger, harbinger, scavenger, porringer. This development may have been merely the addition of n, or it may have resulted due to contamination from other suffixes such as Middle English -ing and the rare Old French -ange, -enc, -inge, -inghe (“-ing”

ex.en: Instead of going myself, I sent a messenger.
ex.ja: 私は自分で行く代わりに、使いの者を送った。

ex.en: Hey, don't blame me. I'm just the messenger.
ex.ja: おい、俺を責めるなよ。俺はただ話を伝えただけなんだから。

ex.en: The messenger left for London in secret.
ex.ja: 使者はひそかにロンドンへ出発した。

note.ja: message（伝言）+ -er。n は後から入った。message はラテン語 mittere（送る）、missus（送られた）から。mission と同じ。

en: A native or inhabitant of Norway.
A kind of fishing boat on the Great Lakes of North America.
Of or pertaining to Norway (the country).
Of or pertaining to the Norwegian people.

Norwegian.ety: From Norwegia + -n or Old English Norweġ + -ian.

ex.en: The English title is "Norwegian Wood".
ex.ja: 英語の題名は「Norwegian Wood」と言います。

ex.en: The Norwegian diplomat mediated the secret negotiations that produced the historic document.
ex.ja: ノルウェー人外交官が、歴史的文書を生んだ秘密交渉を取り持った。

note.ja: Norway（北への道）+ -ian。Norway は north + way。

en: A writing utensil with a graphite (commonly referred to as lead) shaft, usually blended with clay, clad in wood, and sharpened to a taper.
An aggregate or collection of rays of light, especially when diverging from, or converging to, a point.
To write (something) using a pencil.
To mark with, or as if with, a pencil.

pencil.ety: From Anglo-Norman and Old French pincil (see the variant pincel, which gave rise to Modern French pinceau (“paintbrush”)), from Latin pēnicillum, diminutive of pēniculus (“brush”), itself a diminutive of pēnis (“tail; penis”). Not related to pen.

ex.en: Put down your pencil and listen to me.
ex.ja: 鉛筆を置いて私の言うことを聞きなさい。

ex.en: Write with a pen, not with a pencil.
ex.ja: 鉛筆ではなく、ペンで書きなさい。

ex.en: Do you have a pen or a pencil?
ex.ja: ペンか鉛筆を持っていますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 penicillus（小さな尾・絵筆）から。penis（尾）+ 縮小。もとは「絵筆」。penicillin（筆のような形のカビ）も同じ。

en: Of, or pertaining to, philosophy.
Rational; analytic or critically minded; thoughtful.

philosophical.ety: From philosophy + -ical, from Ancient Greek φιλοσοφία (philosophía, “love of knowledge, scientific learning”). Displaced native Old English ūþwitlīċ.

ex.en: He's quite philosophical about his demotion.
ex.ja: 彼は降格されたことを達観している。

note.ja: philosophy + -ical。ギリシャ語 philos（愛する）+ sophia（知恵）。「哲学の」→ 物事を哲学者のように受け止める「達観した」。

en: A state of matter consisting of partially ionized gas and electrons.
A clear component of blood or lymph containing fibrin.
To transform something into plasma.

plasma.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Hellenic *plátʰyō
Proto-Hellenic *plát͏̌t͏̌ō?
Ancient Greek πλάσσω (plássō)
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥
Proto-Hellenic *-mə
Ancient Greek -μα (-ma)
Ancient Greek πλᾰ́σμᾰ (plắsmă)der.
Late Latin plasmader.
English plasma
From Late Latin plasma (“mold”), from Ancient Greek πλάσμα (plásma, “something formed”).

ex.en: Blood is made of plasma and blood cells.
ex.ja: 血液は血漿と血球からできている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 plasma（形作られたもの）から。plassein（形作る）。plastic（形作れる）と同じ。

en: An appeal, petition, urgent prayer or entreaty.
An excuse; an apology.
To plead; to argue.

plea.ety: From Middle English ple, from Old French plait, plaid, from Medieval Latin placitum (“a decree, sentence, suit, plea, etc., Latin an opinion, determination, prescription, order; literally, that which is pleasing, pleasure”), neuter of placitus, past participle of placere (“to please”). Cognate with Spanish pleito (“lawsuit, suit”). Doublet of placit. See also please, pleasure.

ex.en: He was deaf to my pleas.
ex.ja: 彼は僕の訴えを聞こうとしなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 placitum（よしとされたこと）から。plac（喜ばせる）の仲間。→「嘆願・（法廷での）申し立て」。plead（嘆願する）。

en: To cause (a child, student, or someone else being looked after, or a suspect or criminal) to suffer for crime or misconduct, to administe…
To treat harshly and unfairly.

punish.ety: From Middle English punischen, from Anglo-Norman, Old French puniss-, stem of some of the conjugated forms of punir, from Latin puniō (“to inflict punishment upon”), from poena (“punishment, penalty”); see pain. Displaced Old English wītnian and (mostly, in this sense) wrecan.

ex.en: We thought it wrong that you should punish him.
ex.ja: 君が彼を罰するのは筋違いだと思った。

ex.en: If you lie, I'll punish you.
ex.ja: 嘘をつくと罰が当たるよ。

ex.en: In the name of the moon, I shall punish you!
ex.ja: 月に代わってお仕置きよ！

note.ja: ラテン語 punire（罰する）から。poena（罰）。penalty（罰）、pain（痛み）も同じ poena。

en: A small bag for carrying money.
A handbag (small bag usually used by women for carrying various small personal items)
To press (one's lips) in and together so that they protrude.
To draw up or contract into folds or wrinkles; to pucker; to knit.

purse.ety:
From Middle English purs, from Old English purs (“purse”), partly from pusa (“wallet, bag, scrip”) and partly from burse (“pouch, bag”).
Old English pusa comes from Proto-West Germanic *pusō, from Proto-Germanic *pusô (“bag, sack, scrip”), and is cognate with Old High German pfoso (“pouch, purse”), Low German pūse (“purse, bag”), Old Norse posi (“purse, bag”), Danish pose (“purse, bag”). Old English burse comes from Medieval Latin bursa (“leather bag”) (compare English bursar), from Ancient Greek βύρσα (búrsa, “hide, wine-skin”).
Compare also Old French borse (French bourse), Old Saxon bursa (

ex.en: Will you help me look for my purse?
ex.ja: 財布を探すのを手伝ってくれませんか。

ex.en: I had my purse stolen in the bus.
ex.ja: 私はバスの中で財布を盗まれた。

ex.en: I picked up a purse in the street.
ex.ja: 私は往来で財布を拾った。

note.ja: ラテン語 bursa（革の袋）から。bursar（会計係）、reimburse（払い戻す）も同じ。

en: An offensive back whose primary job is to pass the ball in a play.
An offensive back who receives the snap (hike) and then blocks the defense from crossing the line of scrimmage; a blocking back.
To play the position of quarterback.
To lead a team or group; to be primarily responsible for some group project or activity.

quarterback.ety: From quarter + back, in reference to the position in front of the halfback position.

ex.en: The quarterback threw the ball to his teammate.
ex.ja: クォーターバックはチームメイトにボールを投げた。

note.ja: quarter（4分の1）+ back（後衛）。フォワードと後衛の中間にいる選手。

en: Experiencing or exhibiting relief; freed from stress or discomfort.

ex.en: I am very much relieved to know that.
ex.ja: それを聞いてほっとした。

ex.en: I felt much relieved to hear the news.
ex.ja: 私はそのニュースを聞いて大変安心した。

ex.en: She took Chinese medicine, which relieved her symptoms.
ex.ja: 彼女は漢方薬を飲んだ。すると症状が和らいだ。

note.ja: relieve（和らげる）+ -ed。「重荷を取り除かれた」→「ほっとした」。relief と同じ lev。

en: The act of reserving, withholding or keeping back.
The practice of reserving part of the consecrated bread of the Eucharist for the communion of the sick.

reservation.ety: From Middle French reservation, equivalent to reserve + -ation.

ex.en: I'd like to make a reservation for tonight.
ex.ja: 今晩の予約をしたいのですが。

ex.en: I made hotel reservations one month in advance.
ex.ja: 私は１ヶ月早くホテルの予約を取った。

ex.en: I accept the proposal, but with some reservations.
ex.ja: 私は条件付きで提案に同意する。

note.ja: reserve（取っておく）+ -ation。re（後ろに）+ servare（守る）。「取っておくこと」→「予約・留保・居留地」。

en: The art of using language, especially public speaking, as a means to persuade.
Synonym of rhetorical.

rhetoric.ety:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek ῥητορῐκή τέχνη (rhētorĭkḗ tékhnē)ellip.
Ancient Greek ῥητορικὴ (rhētorikḕ)bor.
Latin rhētoricabor.
Old French rhetoriquebor.
Middle English rhetorik, rhetoric
English rhetoric
Inherited from Middle English rhetorik, rhetoric, borrowed from Old French rhetorique, borrowed from Latin rhētorica, borrowed from Ancient Greek ῥητορικὴ (rhētorikḕ), ellipsis of ῥητορῐκή τέχνη (rhētorĭkḗ tékhnē).

ex.en: The speech was full of empty rhetoric.
ex.ja: その演説は中身のない美辞麗句ばかりだった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 rhētōr（演説家）から。「演説の技術」→「修辞（学）」。

en: The process of being saved, the state of having been saved (from hell).
The act of saving, rescuing (in any context), providing needed safety or liberation; something that does this.

salvation.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *solh₂-der.
Proto-Italic *sal(V)wos
Latin salvus
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu.
Proto-Italic *-ājō
Proto-Italic *-āō
Latin -ō
Latin salvō
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Latin salvātiō
Old French salvacionbor.
Middle English savacioun
English salvation
From Middle English savacioun, from Old French savaciun, salvaciun, from Latin salvātiō. Displaced native Old English hǣlu.

ex.en: "God is our salvation," said the priest.
ex.ja: 「神はわれらの救いである」と司祭は言った。

note.ja: ラテン語 salvare（救う）から。salvus（無事な）。save、safe も同じ。

en: An approval, by an authority, generally one that makes something valid.
A penalty, punishment, or some coercive measure, intended to ensure compliance; especially one adopted by several nations, or by an inter…
To ratify; to make valid.
To give official authorization or approval to; to countenance.

sanction.ety: From Middle French sanction, from Latin sānctiō.

ex.en: That requires the sanction of the government.
ex.ja: それは政府の認可が必要です。

ex.en: The U. N. moved to impose sanctions.
ex.ja: 国連は制裁を加えるために動き出しました。

ex.en: It is necessary to obtain the sanction of the authorities to enter this building.
ex.ja: この建物に入るには当局の許可を得る必要がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 sancire（神聖なものとして定める）から。sanct（聖なる）+ ion。→「認可・（違反への）制裁」。

en: Not specifically religious; lay or civil, as opposed to clerical.
Temporal; worldly, or otherwise not based on something timeless.
A secular ecclesiastic, or one not bound by monastic rules.
A church official whose functions are confined to the vocal department of the choir.

secular.ety: From Middle English seculer, from Old French seculer, from Latin saeculāris (“of the age”), from saeculum.

ex.en: France is a secular country.
ex.ja: フランスは政教分離の国だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 saeculum（世代・世俗）から。→「世俗の・非宗教的な」。

en: The quality or state of being sensitive; sensitiveness.
The ability of an organism or organ to respond to external stimuli.

ex.en: I recommend earmuffs to help with your noise sensitivity.
ex.ja: 聴覚過敏にはイヤーマフがオススメです。

ex.en: I could never match Tom's sensitivity.
ex.ja: トムの繊細な感受性にはかなわない。

ex.en: I am touched by the girl's acute sensitivity.
ex.ja: 少女の鋭い感性に触れている。

note.ja: sensitive（敏感な）+ -ity。ラテン語 sentire（感じる）。sense と同じ sens。

en: To inhale a larger quantity of air than usual, and immediately expel it; to make a deep single audible respiration, especially as the res…
To lament; to grieve.
A deep, prolonged audible inhale and exhale of breath; as when fatigued, frustrated, grieved, or relieved; the act of sighing.
a manifestation of grief; a lament.
An expression of fatigue, exhaustion, grief, sorrow, frustration, or the like, often used in casual written contexts.

sigh.ety: From Middle English sighen (“to sigh”), back-formation from sighte, past tense form of siken, from Old English sīcan, from Proto-West Germanic *sīkan, perhaps ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *seykʷ- (“to pour out”).

ex.en: With a sigh, the boys left one another.
ex.ja: ため息をつくと、男子たちは散っていった。

ex.en: Once outside, I gave a deep sigh of relief.
ex.ja: 外へ出ると、私は深深と安堵のため息をついた。

ex.en: I sighed with relief to hear it.
ex.ja: それを聞いて安心の吐息をはいた。

note.ja: 古英語 sīcan（ため息をつく）から。擬音的な語。

en: The cardinal number occurring after fifteen and before seventeen, represented in Arabic numerals as 16 and in Roman numerals as XVI.

sixteen.ety: Inherited from Middle English sextene, sixtene, from Old English sixtīene, from Proto-Germanic *sehstehun. Cognate with West Frisian sechstjin, Dutch zestien, German sechzehn, Danish seksten. Equivalent to six + -teen.

ex.en: Now you are sixteen, you should know better.
ex.ja: もう１６歳なのだから、もっと分別をもちなさいよ。

ex.en: I will be sixteen years old next year.
ex.ja: 来年16歳になります。

ex.en: She said he would be sixteen next month.
ex.ja: 彼女は来月１６歳になると言った。

en: Exercising power of rule.
Having supreme, ultimate power; (often specifically, of a polity) having fully independent power in international relations.
A monarch: a supreme ruler of a country in a monarchical system.
One who is not a subject to a ruler or nation.
To rule over as a sovereign.

sovereign.ety: From Middle English sovereyn, from Old French soverain (whence also modern French souverain), from Vulgar Latin *superānus (compare Italian sovrano, Spanish soberano) from Latin super (“above”). Spelling influenced by folk-etymology association with reign. Doublet of soprano, from the same Latin root via Italian. Doublet of souverain. See also suzerain, foreign.

ex.en: Queen Victoria was the sovereign of Great Britain.
ex.ja: ビクトリア女王は英国の君主だった。

ex.en: Citizens are the ultimate sovereigns.
ex.ja: 市民は最高の主権者である。

ex.en: The sovereign completely recovered from his illness.
ex.ja: 君主は病気から完全に回復した。

note.ja: ラテン語 superanus（上にいる者）から。super（上に）。「最上位の者」→「君主・主権を持つ」。g は綴りに入った飾りで発音しない。

en: A person in a marriage or marital relationship.

spouse.ety:
From Middle English spous, spouse, from Anglo-Norman espus m, espuse f and Old French espos m, espose f and by aphesis from Latin spōnsus m (“bridegroom”), spōnsa f (“bride”), from spondeō (“to vow, pledge”), from Proto-Indo-European *spend-. Displaced native Old English ġemaca.
Related to espouse and sponsor.

ex.en: She was an excellent spouse who stood by him through poverty.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼が貧しいときも彼を支えるすばらしい配偶者だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 sponsus（婚約した人）から。spondere（誓う）。「誓いを交わした相手」→「配偶者」。respond、sponsor も同じ spond。

en: A person with the official task of overseeing the work of a person or group, or of other operations and activities.
A person who monitors someone to make sure they comply with rules or other requirements set for them.

supervisor.ety: Attested since the 15th century C.E.; from Middle English supervisor, supervisour, supervysor, supervysour, from Latin supervīsor, from supervideō, in turn from super + videō. By surface analysis, supervise + -or.

ex.en: If it gets that bad, replace the supervisor.
ex.ja: ほんとにまずいなら監督交代だよ。

ex.en: You must act under the leadership of your supervisor.
ex.ja: 監督に従って行動しなくてはいけない。

ex.en: The supervisor bought a really fast machine.
ex.ja: 部長が、すごいハイスペック・マシン買ったそうよ。

note.ja: super（上から）+ vis（見る）+ or（人）。上から見る人 →「監督者・上司」。

en: Of, or relating to synthesis.
Produced by synthesis instead of being isolated from a natural source (but may be identical to a product so obtained).
A synthetic compound.

According to one theory the term is derived from Hobin, a pet name of Robert or Robin, at the time frequently used as a proper name for a workhorse (compare dobbin).
Alternatively, possibly from Anglo-Norman hobyn, Old French hobin, obin ("a nag, hobby"; > Modern French aubin, Italian ubino): either derived from Old French hober, ober (“to stir, move”), from Old Dutch *hobbon ("to toss, move up and down"; whence Middle Dutch hobbelen (“to bump along”));

note.ja: hobby-horse（棒の先に馬の頭をつけたおもちゃ）の短縮。「おもちゃの馬で遊ぶこと」→「趣味」。

Cognate with German schwappen (“to slosh, slop”). ex.en: With which things do you want to swap?
ex.ja: どれとどれを交換する？

note.ja: 中英語 swappen（打つ）から。取引で手を打ち合わせたことから「交換する」。

en: A single, distinctive rock formation; an area having a preponderance of a particular rock or group of rocks.
An area of land or its particular features.

terrain.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French terrain, from Latin terrenum (“land, ground”), neuter of terrenus (“consisting of earth”), from terra (“earth”).

ex.en: The bike is designed for rough terrain.
ex.ja: その自転車は険しい地形を走れるように作られている。

note.ja: ラテン語 terra（大地）から。→「地形・地域」。territory（領土）も同じ terr。

en: Extremely frightened.

ex.en: The man terrified the little children.
ex.ja: 男は小さな子供たちを怖がらせた。

ex.en: She looked away terrified.
ex.ja: 彼女は恐くて目をそらした。

ex.en: Tom is obviously terrified.
ex.ja: トムは見るからに怖がっている。

note.ja: terrify（怖がらせる）+ -ed。ラテン語 terrere（震えさせる）。「おびえた」。terror と同じ。

en: Extremely excited or delighted.

ex.en: I am thrilled with my new home.
ex.ja: 自分の新居にわくわくしている。

ex.en: Everybody was thrilled by his story.
ex.ja: みんな彼の話にわくわくした。

ex.ja: その映画はすべての観客をぞくぞくさせた。

note.ja: thrill（ぞくぞくさせる）+ -ed。thrill は古英語 thyrlian（穴をあける）、「突き通す」→「ぞくぞくさせる」。

en: A cloth used for wiping, especially one used for drying anything wet, such as a person after a bath.
To dry by using a towel.
To hit with a towel.

towel.ety: From Middle English towayle, towel, towail, towaille, from Old French toaille (“towel”) (modern French touaille), Medieval Latin toallia, from Frankish *þwahilu (“cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *þwahaną (“to wash”). Cognate with Old High German dwahila (“towel”) (modern dialectal German Zwehle), Dutch dwaal (“towel”), dweil (“mop”), Low German Dweel (“towel”), Old English þwǣle (“band; ribbon; fillet”), Old English þwēan (“to wash”).

ex.en: Could you bring me another hot towel?
ex.ja: おしぼりをもう一本ください。

ex.en: The towels in the bathroom are dirty.
ex.ja: 洗面所のタオルが汚れています。

ex.en: The towel on the left is yours.
ex.ja: 左のタオルが、あなたのよ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 toaille（布）から。ゲルマン系で「洗う・拭く」。

en: A group of three people or things.
A group of three musicians.

trio.ety:

ex.ja: レストランではジャズトリオが演奏していた。

note.ja: イタリア語 trio。tri（3つの）から。duo（2）、quartet（4）と並ぶ。

en: Not awake; having no awareness (usually as the result of a head injury).
Without directed thought or awareness.
That part of mind that is not consciously perceived.

ex.ja: トムは台所の床で意識を失って倒れているメアリーを発見した。

ex.ja: その情報は二人の記者によって確認された。

note.ja: verify（確かめる）+ -ed。ラテン語 verus（真実の）+ facere。「本当だと確かめられた」。very と同じ ver。

en: An atmosphere or aura felt to belong to a person, place or thing.
Gut feeling, an impression based on intuition instead of solid data.
To stimulate with a vibrator.
To relax and enjoy oneself.

vibe.ety: Apocopic form of vibration, vibrator, etc.

ex.en: I love stuff with this sort of futuristic vibe.
ex.ja: こういう未来感あるの大好き。

note.ja: vibration（振動）の短縮。「伝わってくる振動」→「雰囲気・ノリ」。vibrate。

en: The idea of all that is good or excellent (in every sense of those terms) in a human being, collectively instantiated by a varying number…
Accordance with moral principles; conformity of behaviour or thought with the strictures of morality; good moral conduct.

virtue.ety: From Middle English vertu, virtue, borrowed from Anglo-Norman vertu, virtu, from Latin virtus (“manliness, bravery, worth, moral excellence”), from vir (“man”). Doublet of vertu. See virile. In this sense, displaced Old English cræft, whence Modern English craft.

ex.en: Your plan has the virtue of being practical.
ex.ja: あなたの計画は実際的だという長所がある。

ex.en: It is a virtue never to tell a lie.
ex.ja: 決してうそをつかないことは美徳である。

ex.en: I can tell virtue and vice apart.
ex.ja: 私には美徳と悪徳との区別がつく。

note.ja: ラテン語 virtus（男らしさ・勇気）から。vir（男）。→「美徳・長所」。virtual（実質上の：力のある）も同じ。

en: All the workers employed by a specific organization or state, or on a specific project.
The total population of a country or region that is employed or employable.

ex.en: "Black companies" are avoided by the workforce.
ex.ja: ブラック企業は労働者から敬遠されます。

ex.en: Exploitative companies are avoided by the workforce.
ex.ja: ブラック企業は労働者から敬遠されます。

note.ja: work（労働）+ force（力）。「働く力」→「労働力」。

A dead person, reanimated through some fictional agency as a fungus, virus, or the like, that has an insatiable desire to eat living huma…

zombie.ety: First attested in the 18th century. Partially through Louisiana Creole zombi (“zombie; ghost”), Haitian Creole zonbi (“zombie”), and French zombi (“zombie”). Ultimately from a Bantu language. Compare Kongo nzambi (“god”), zumbi (“fetish”), and Kimbundu nzumbi (“ghost”) (see Portuguese zumbi, Sranan Tongo dyumbi), and Caribbean folklore's jumbie (“a spirit or demon”).

ex.en: After my husband's death I walked around like a zombie.
ex.ja: 夫の死後私はゾンビのようにふらふら歩き回っていた。

ex.en: I was bitten by a zombie.
ex.ja: ゾンビに噛まれた。

ex.en: I wonder which one I'll watch, the zombie one or the vampire one.
ex.ja: ゾンビものと吸血鬼もの、どっちを観るかなあ。

note.ja: 西アフリカ・ハイチの言葉 nzambi（神・霊）から。

en: At the end of a religious prayer: so be it.
Used to indicate emphatic agreement.
Certainly; verily.
An instance of saying ‘amen’.
To say amen.
To say amen to; to ratify solemnly.

amen.ety:

Inherited from Middle English amen, from Old English āmen, from Ecclesiastical Latin āmēn, from Ancient Greek ἀμήν (amḗn), from Biblical Hebrew אָמֵן (ʾāmēn, “certainly, verily”) (cognate with Arabic آمِينَ (ʔāmīna), Classical Syriac ܐܡܝܢ (ʾāmên)).
In Old English, it was used only at the end of the Gospels; elsewhere, it was translated as sōþlīċe! (“truly, indeed!”), swā hit is (“so it is”), and sīe! (“[so] be it!”).

ex.en: At the end of the prayer, everyone said "Amen."
ex.ja: 祈りの終わりに、全員が「アーメン」と言った。

note.ja: ヘブライ語で「確かに・そうでありますように」。祈りの結びの言葉。

en: To come up from a lower to a higher position.
To come up from one's bed or place of repose; to get up.

arise.ety: From Middle English arisen, from Old English ārīsan (“to arise, get up; rise; spring from, originate; spring up, ascend”), from Proto-Germanic *uzrīsaną (“to rise up, arise”), equivalent to a- + rise. Cognate with Scots arise, aryse (“to arise, rise up, come into existence”), Middle Low German errīsen (“to stand up, arise”), Old High German irrīsan (“to rise up, fall”), Gothic 𐌿𐍂𐍂𐌴𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽 (urreisan, “to arise”). Eclipsed Middle English sourden, sorden, borrowed from Old French sordre, sourdre (“to arise, originate, fly up”).

ex.en: A conflict of opinions arose over the matter.
ex.ja: その問題で意見の衝突が起きた。

ex.en: When we think this way, many problems arise.
ex.ja: このように考えると多くの問題が起きてくる。

ex.en: You should change your job if the occasion arises.
ex.ja: 機会があれば職を変えるべきだ。

note.ja: 古英語 ārīsan ＝ a（上へ）+ rise。「起こる・生じる」。

ex.ja: 敵は戦場からちりぢりに逃げ去った。

en: A blossom; the flower of a plant; an expanded bud.
Flowers.
To cause to blossom; to make flourish.
To bestow a bloom upon; to make blooming or radiant.

bloom.ety: From Middle English blome, from Old Norse blóm, from Proto-Germanic *blōmô (“flower”). Doublet of bloom (“spongy mass of metal”); see there for more.

ex.en: Musical talent usually blooms at an early age.
ex.ja: 音楽の才能は普通早く開花する。

ex.en: The flowers in the garden bloom in spring.
ex.ja: 庭の花は春に咲きます。

ex.ja: この花は他の花より早く咲くんだ。

note.ja: 古北欧語 blóm（花）から。blossom、flower と同じ祖先。「花・咲く」。

en: A group of objects held together by wrapping or tying.
A package wrapped or tied up for carrying.
To tie or wrap together into a bundle.
To hustle; to dispatch something or someone quickly.

bundle.ety: From Middle English bundel, from Middle Dutch bondel or Old English byndele, byndelle (“a binding; tying; fastening with bands”); both from Proto-Germanic *bundil-, derivative of *bundą (“bundle”). Compare also bindle, Dutch bundel, German Bündel.

ex.en: That kid is a little bundle of energy.
ex.ja: その子どもは元気そのものです。

ex.ja: 彼は古い手紙を束にした。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 bundel（束）から。bind（縛る）と同じ祖先。「縛ったもの」→「束」。

en: Something that happens by chance, especially an unfortunate event; an accident, a disaster.
A person suffering from injuries or who has been killed due to an accident or through an act of violence.

casualty.ety: From casual, from Middle French casuel, from Medieval Latin casualitas and Late Latin cāsuālis (“happening by chance”), from Latin cāsus (“event”) (English case), from cadere (“to fall”). ex.en: The clown made a funny face.
ex.ja: 道化師はこっけいな顔をした。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。16世紀ごろの「田舎者」→「道化師」。

conjunction.ety: From Old French conjonction, from Latin coniūnctiō (“joining”), from coniungere (“to join”).

ex.en: "And" and "but" are common conjunctions.
ex.ja: 「and」や「but」はよく使われる接続詞だ。

costly.ety: From Middle English costly, costely, costeley, equivalent to cost + -ly.

ex.en: This computer will prove costly in the long run.
ex.ja: このコンピューターは、長い目で見れば高くつく。

ex.ja: どうしてそんなに高い辞書を買いましたか。

A way down.

descent.ety: From Middle English and Anglo-Norman descente, from Anglo-Norman descendre (“to descend”); see descend. Compare ascent, ascend. Doublet of desant.

ex.ja: 私は頂上から下山する途中彼らに会った。

ex.ja: トムはドイツ系のアメリカ人です。

A desktop computer.
Designed for use on a desk or similar piece of furniture.

ex.en: Of course desktops are more efficient.
ex.ja: やっぱりデスクトップの方が効率的。

Such a field as part of a clock face; (metonymic) the entire clock face.

ex.ja: ダイヤル式の電話って、ほとんど見なくなったな。

en: A list of names, addresses etc, of specific classes of people or organizations, often in alphabetical order or in some classification.
A structured listing of the names and characteristics of the files on a storage device.
Containing directions; instructing; directorial.

directory.ety: From Middle English directorie, dyrectorye, from Medieval Latin dīrēctōrium. By surface analysis, direct + -ory. Doublet of directorium. The political sense is a semantic loan from French directoire.

ex.en: You can find her phone number in the directory.
ex.ja: 彼女の電話番号は電話帳でわかりますよ。

ex.en: I looked up his telephone number in a telephone directory.
ex.ja: 私は電話帳で彼の電話番号を調べた。

ex.en: May I see the telephone directory?
ex.ja: 電話帳をみせてもらえますか。

To free of a debt, claim, obligation, responsibility, accusation, etc.; to absolve; to acquit; to forgive; to clear.
The act of releasing an inpatient from hospital.
The act of releasing a member of the armed forces from service.

discharge.ety: From Middle English dischargen, from Old French deschargier (“to unload”), from Late Latin discarricāre (“unload”). By surface analysis, dis- + charge.

ex.en: I have a discharge from my left ear.
ex.ja: 左耳から耳だれが出ます。

ex.en: When the work was done, the men were discharged.
ex.ja: その仕事が終わると男達は解雇された。

ex.ja: 患者は退院した。

To avoid; to sidestep.
An act of dodging.
A trick, evasion or wile. (Now mainly in the expression tax dodge.)
Dodgy.

dodge.ety: Likely from dialectal dodge, dod, dodd (“to jog, trudge along, totter", also "to jerk, jig”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from unrecorded Middle English *dodden, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *dud- (“to move”), related to Old English dydrian, dyderian (“to delude, deceive”), Middle English dideren (“to tremble, quake, shiver”), English dodder, Norwegian dudra (“to tremble”).

ex.en: Don't dodge the issue, I want you to answer my question.
ex.ja: はぐらかさないで、俺の質問に答えて欲しいんです。

ex.en: Tom decided not to play dodge ball because he wasn't feeling well.
ex.ja: 体調が悪かったので、トムはドッジボールをしないことにした。

ex.en: I was somehow able to dodge the attack with ease.
ex.ja: なんとか上手く攻撃をかわした。

note.ja: 語源は不詳。16世紀から「さっと身をかわす」。

en: The act of eliminating, expelling or throwing off.
The act of excluding a losing contestant from a match, tournament, or other competition.

elimination.ety: Borrowed from Latin ēliminātiō, from eliminate + -ion.

ex.en: "Why me?" "Because, by process of elimination, there was no other choice."
ex.ja: 「なんで私？」「消去法で仕方がなかったから」

ex.en: The 21st March is the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.
ex.ja: 3月21日は国際人種差別撤廃デーです。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ limen（敷居）+ -ation。「敷居の外へ出すこと」→「除去・排除・敗退」。eliminate。

en: The pungent aromatic rhizome of a tropical Asian herb, Zingiber officinale, used as a spice and as a stimulant and acarminative.
The plant that produces this rhizome.
Of a reddish-brown color.
Having hair or fur of this color.
To add ginger to.
To enliven, to spice (up).
In a very careful or cautious manner; also, delicately, sensitively.

ex.en: Do you like ginger?
ex.ja: 生姜って、好き？

ex.en: Do you like ginger ale?
ex.ja: ジンジャーエールは好きですか？

ex.en: Sushi is often served with pickled ginger.
ex.ja: お寿司にはよく甘酢生姜が添えられています。

note.ja: サンスクリット語 śṛṅgavera（角の形の根）から、ギリシャ語・ラテン語を経た語。根の色から「赤毛」。

en: A group or association mainly of tradespeople made up of merchants, craftspeople, or artisans, particularly in the Middle Ages, establish…
A corporation.

guild.ety: From Middle English gilde, from Old Norse gildi (“payment, guild”). Related to geld, yield, yauld.

ex.en: The writers formed a guild to protect their rights.
ex.ja: 作家たちは自分たちの権利を守るために組合を作った。

note.ja: 古英語 gild（支払い）から。「会費を払って入る会」→「同業組合」。

en: To stop marching.
To stop either temporarily or permanently.

halt.ety: From Middle French halt, from early modern German halt (“stop!”), imperative of halten (“to hold, to stop”). Doublet of hold (see that entry for more information).

ex.en: The train was brought to a sudden halt.
ex.ja: 汽車は突然止まった。

ex.en: Traffic was halted for several hours.
ex.ja: 事故で交通は数時間止められた。

ex.en: Then, the train screeched to a halt.
ex.ja: そして、電車はキーッという音を立てて止まった。

note.ja: ドイツ語 halten（止まる）から。hold（保つ）と同じ祖先。軍隊の号令 Halt!（止まれ）。

en: Lack of the ability to do something; incapability.
Lack of the option to do something; powerlessness.

inability.ety: From earlier inhability (“disqualification for office”), equivalent to in- + ability. Compare Middle French inhabilité, Medieval Latin inhabilitās.

ex.en: I am impatient with his inability to make decisions.
ex.ja: 彼が決断できないのに私はしびれをきらしている。

ex.en: I was surprised at her inability to do things promptly.
ex.ja: 彼女が物事をてきぱきできないのを驚いた。

ex.en: Superstitions derive from the inability of men to acknowledge that coincidences are merely coincidences.
ex.ja: 迷信というのは、偶然はただの偶然なのだと、人間が理解できないことから生じる。

note.ja: in（否定）+ ability（能力）。「できないこと」。

en: Coming (or about to come) in; arriving.
Succeeding to an office or other position.
A warning that something is coming towards the addressee, especially enemy artillery fire.
The act of coming in; arrival.
Enemy fire directed at oneself.

ex.en: The incoming president will take office in January.
ex.ja: 次期大統領は１月に就任する。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ coming（来る）。「入ってくる・次期の」。outgoing の対。

en: An earthenware container, either with two or no handles, for holding oil, water, wine, etc., or used for burial.
A small, approximately cylindrical container, normally made of clay or glass, for holding fruit, preserves, etc., or for ornamental purpo…
To preserve (food) in a jar.

jar.ety:
Inherited from Middle English jarre (“jar”), from Medieval Latin jarra, or from Middle French jarre (“liquid measure”) (from Old French jare; modern French jarre (“earthenware jar”)), or from Spanish jarra, jarro (“jug, pitcher; mug, stein”), all from Arabic جَرَّة (jarra, “earthen receptacle”).
The word is cognate with Italian giara (“jar; crock”), Occitan jarro, Portuguese jarra, jarro (“jug; ewer, pitcher”).
The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: Is there much sugar in the jar?
ex.ja: つぼにたくさん砂糖が入っていますか。

ex.en: I wanted some salt, but there was none in the jar.
ex.ja: 塩が欲しかったが、ビンの中には少しもなかった。

ex.en: Fill the jars with water.
ex.ja: 水瓶に水を満たしなさい。

note.ja: アラビア語 jarra（土器のつぼ）から。

en: The conduct of a lawsuit.

litigation.ety: Borrowed from Latin lītigātiō, equivalent to litigate + -ion.

ex.en: The two companies avoided costly litigation.
ex.ja: 二つの会社は費用のかかる訴訟を避けた。

note.ja: ラテン語 litigare（争う）から。lis（争い）+ agere（行う）。「争いを行うこと」→「訴訟」。

en: A wise and trusted counselor or teacher.
To act as someone's mentor.

mentor.ety: From French mentor, from Ancient Greek Μέντωρ (Méntōr, “Mentor”), a mythological character in the Odyssey, whose name, a historical name from Ancient Greece, shares the same root as English mind. Cognate to Sanskrit मन्तृ (mantṛ, “advisor, counselor”) and Latin monitor (“one who admonishes”), and perhaps ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *monéyeti (compare Latin moneō (“to warn”), causative form of *men- (“to think”).

ex.en: You have been a great mentor to me.
ex.ja: 貴殿には、いろいろ御指導いただきました。

note.ja: ギリシャ神話『オデュッセイア』で、オデュッセウスの息子を導いた老人メントル（Mentor）の名から。「よき指導者」。

en: Goods which are or were offered or intended for sale.
Commercial goods connected (branded) with an entity such as a team, band, company, charity, work of fiction, festival, or meme. (Commonly…
To engage in in-store promotion of the sale of goods, as by display and arrangement of goods.
To engage in in-store promotion of the sale of.

ex.en: Should we send back the wrong merchandise?
ex.ja: 間違った商品を送り返しましょうか。

ex.en: I saw somebody steal the merchandise.
ex.ja: 誰かがその商品を盗むのを見たんです。

ex.en: The supermarket has a large stock of merchandise.
ex.ja: そのスーパーマーケットは大量の商品在庫を持っている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 marchandise（商品）から。marchand（商人）。merchant と同じ merc。

en: A person who works in a mine.
An operator of ordnance mines and similar explosives.

miner.ety: From mine + -er (agent noun suffix) or + -er (occupational suffix).

ex.en: The miners went on strike for a wage increase.
ex.ja: 鉱山労働者が賃上げを要求してストに突入した。

ex.en: I was a miner for two years.
ex.ja: ２年間、鉱山作業員だったんだ。

ex.en: That branch is affiliated to the miners' union.
ex.ja: あの支部は炭鉱労働組合に属している。

note.ja: mine（鉱山・掘る）+ -er。「鉱山で掘る人」。

en: A male member of a monastic order who has devoted his life for religious service.
In earlier usage, an eremite or hermit devoted to solitude, as opposed to a cenobite, who lived communally.
To be a monk.
To act like a monk; especially to be contemplative.

monk.ety: From Middle English monk, from Old English munuc, from Proto-West Germanic *munik, from Late Latin monicus, variant of monachus, from Ancient Greek μοναχός (monakhós, “single, solitary”), from μόνος (mónos, “alone”).

ex.en: Tom is a monk, isn't he?
ex.ja: トムって、お坊さんなんだよね？

ex.en: Monks used to play tennis in monasteries.
ex.ja: 当時は修道僧達が修道院でよくテニスをしていた。

ex.en: He practices austerities almost like a monk.
ex.ja: 彼は僧侶に近い禁欲生活をしている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 monachos（一人で暮らす人）から。monos（1つの・一人の）。mono-、monastery（修道院）と同じ。

en: That which is normal or typical.
A rule that is imposed by regulations and/or socially enforced by members of a community.
To endow (a vector space, etc.) with a norm.

norm.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-sḱéti
Proto-Indo-European *ǵn̥h₃sḱétider.
Proto-Hellenic *gignṓskō
Ancient Greek γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō)

Etruscanbor.?
Latin normabor.
English norm
From Latin norma (“a carpenter's square, a rule, a pattern, a precept”). Doublet of norma.

ex.en: Her behaviour towards me was a departure from the norm.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に対する態度がいつもと違っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 norma（大工の直角定規）から。→「規範・標準」。normal（普通の）、enormous（並外れた）も同じ。

ex.en: I was offended at his behavior.
ex.ja: 彼の振る舞いに腹が立った。

ex.en: His way of speaking offended me.
ex.ja: 彼の話ぶりに腹が立った。

ex.en: She seems to have been offended by what he said.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の言葉に気を悪くしたようだ。

note.ja: offend（怒らせる）+ -ed。「気分を害した」。

en: Conforming to the accepted, established, or traditional doctrines of a given faith, religion, or ideology.
Adhering to whatever is customary, traditional, or generally accepted.

orthodox.ety: From Late Middle English orthodoxe, from Middle French orthodoxe and its etymon Late Latin orthodoxus, from Ancient Greek ὀρθόδοξος (orthódoxos), from ὀρθός (orthós, “straight”) + δόξα (dóxa, “opinion”). Displaced native Old English wuldorlīċ.

ex.en: The doctor prefers orthodox treatments.
ex.ja: その医師は伝統的な治療法を好む。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 orthos（正しい）+ doxa（意見）。「正しい考え」→「正統な」。orthodontist（歯並びを正す医者）と同じ ortho。

en: Located above, especially over the head.
Kicked over one's own head.
The expense of a business not directly assigned to goods or services provided.
The items or classes of expense not directly assigned to goods or services provided.
Above one's head; in the sky.
Above.

overhead.ety: From Middle English owerheved, over-hed, over hede (adverb), from Old English oferhēafod (adverb), equivalent to over- + head. Compare German Low German overhoopt, överhoopt, German überhaupt. Piecewise doublet of overchief.

ex.en: A couple of swallows are flying overhead.
ex.ja: つばめが二羽頭上を飛んでいる。

ex.en: Should I put this bag in the overhead compartment?
ex.ja: このバッグは上の棚に入れた方がいいですか。

ex.en: It's in the overhead compartment.
ex.ja: お席の上の棚の中に入っております。

note.ja: over（上の）+ head（頭）。「頭上の」→ 会社の上にかかる「間接費」。

en: An artist who paints pictures.
A laborer or workman who paints surfaces using a paintbrush or other means.

painter.ety: Inherited from Middle English peyntour, from Old French peintor, equivalent to paint + -er.

ex.en: The picture was painted by a famous painter.
ex.ja: この絵はある有名な画家によってかかれた。

ex.en: He has a great talent as a painter.
ex.ja: 彼は画家として大変な才能がある。

ex.en: He thinks he is something of a painter.
ex.ja: 彼は自分がちょっとした画家だと思っている。

note.ja: paint（描く・塗る）+ -er。「画家・ペンキ屋」。

en: To puncture; to break through.
To create a hole in the skin for the purpose of inserting jewelry.
A pierced earring.

pierce.ety: From Middle English perce, from conjugated forms of Old French percier such as (jeo) pierce (“I pierce”), probably from Vulgar Latin *pertūsiō, from Latin pertūsus, past participle of pertundō (“thrust or bore through”), from per- (“through”) + tundō (“beat, pound”). Displaced native Old English þȳrlian (literally “to hole”).

ex.en: His words pierced to the heart of the matter.
ex.ja: 彼の言葉は問題の核心に触れるものだった。

ex.en: I want to get my ears pierced.
ex.ja: 耳にピアス開けたいのよ。

ex.en: Tom has a pierced ear.
ex.ja: トムは耳にピアスをしています。

note.ja: 古フランス語 percer（穴をあける）から。per（通して）とラテン語 tundere（打つ）が由来とされる。

en: A handgun
The type of handgun with the chamber integral with the barrel.
To shoot (at) a target with a pistol.

pistol.ety:
Probably from Middle French pistole, or via Middle English pistolet, from Middle French pistolet (“small firearm or small dagger”).
The origin is unclear.
If via German to Romance probably from Middle High German forms like pischulle from Czech píšťala (“firearm”, literally “tube, pipe”), from Proto-Slavic *piščalь, from *piskati, *piščati (“to squeak, whistle”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pīṣk-.
Alternatively, if from Romance to German, from or related to Italian pistolese (“short dagger”), from Italian Pistoia (“a Tuscan town noted for its gunsmithing”).

ex.en: He reached for the pistol.
ex.ja: 彼はピストルを取ろうと手を伸ばした。

ex.en: I heard a pistol shot.
ex.ja: 銃の音を聞いた。

ex.en: Bill was careless in handling his pistol.
ex.ja: ビルはピストルの扱いに不注意だった。

note.ja: チェコ語 píšťala（笛・管）からドイツ語を経た語。管の形から。

en: One who makes prints.
The operator of a printing press or the owner of a printing business; (metonymic) any printing business.

ex.en: Don't you plan to buy a new printer?
ex.ja: 新しいプリンターを買う予定はないですか？

ex.en: Aren't you planning to buy a new printer?
ex.ja: 新しいプリンターを買う予定はないですか？

ex.en: Are you planning to buy a new printer?
ex.ja: 新しいプリンターを買う予定はないですか？

note.ja: print（印刷する）+ -er。「印刷機・印刷業者」。

en: Lying face-down.
Of the hand, forearm or foot: turned facing away from the body; with the thumb inward or big toe downward.
To place in a prone position, to place face down.

prone.ety: From Middle English prone, proone, proon, from Latin prōnus (“turned forward, bent or inclined”), from prō (“forward”).

ex.en: He is prone to getting excited.
ex.ja: 彼は興奮しやすい。

ex.en: Young people are prone to fall into temptation.
ex.ja: 若い人たちは誘惑に陥りやすい。

ex.en: Young men are prone to fall into temptation.
ex.ja: 若い人は誘惑に陥りがちである。

note.ja: ラテン語 pronus（前に傾いた）から。「うつぶせの」→「〜の傾向がある・しがちな」。

en: Without unwillingness or hesitation; showing readiness.
Without impediment, easily.

readily.ety: From Middle English redily, rediliche. By surface analysis, read(i) + -ly.

ex.en: I'm not going to agree to your proposal so readily.
ex.ja: きみの案にはそうやすやすと賛成できない。

ex.en: He readily agreed to my proposal.
ex.ja: 彼は進んで私の提案に賛成した。

ex.en: She readily agreed to my proposal.
ex.ja: 彼女は進んで私の提案に賛成した。

note.ja: ready（準備のできた）+ -ly。「すぐ用意ができて」→「すぐに・快く」。

en: A unit of armed troops under the command of an officer, and consisting of several smaller units.
To form soldiers into a regiment.
To systematize, or put in rigid order.

regiment.ety: From Middle French regement, régiment, and its source, Late Latin regimentum (“direction for government; course of medical treatment”), from Latin regō (“rule”).

ex.en: My grandfather served in an army regiment.
ex.ja: 私の祖父は陸軍の連隊に所属していた。

note.ja: ラテン語 regimentum（統治）から。regere（治める）。「統率された部隊」→「連隊」。regime と同じ。

en: The process or act of reuniting.
A planned event at which members of a dispersed group meet together.

reunion.ety: From Middle French reunion (modern French réunion). By surface analysis, re- + union. Doublet of Réunion.

ex.en: We fixed the date for our class reunion.
ex.ja: 同窓会の日取りを決めた。

ex.en: We've decided the date for our class reunion.
ex.ja: 同窓会の日取りを決めた。

ex.en: We've set the date for our class reunion.
ex.ja: 同窓会の日取りを決めた。

note.ja: re（再び）+ union（結合）。「再会・同窓会」。

en: The act of reviving, or the state of being revived.
Reanimation from a state of languor or depression; applied to health, a person's spirits, etc.

revival.ety:

ex.en: The old musical is enjoying a revival this year.
ex.ja: その古いミュージカルが今年再上演されて人気を集めている。

en: A place of safety, refuge, or protection.
An area set aside for protection.

sanctuary.ety: From Middle English seyntuarie, from Old French saintuaire, from Late Latin sanctuarium (“a sacred place, a shrine, a private cabinet, in Medieval Latin also temple, church, churchyard, cemetery, right of asylum”), from Latin sanctus (“holy, sacred”); see saint.

ex.en: The island is a sanctuary for wild birds.
ex.ja: その島は野鳥の保護区になっている。

note.ja: ラテン語 sanctus（聖なる）から。聖なる場所 →「聖域・避難所・保護区」。

en: A device or organ that detects certain external stimuli and responds in a distinctive manner.

sensor.ety: Originated 1925–30, formed as a Latin loanword from sentiō (“to feel”) + -tor (“-er”). By surface analysis, sense + -or.

ex.en: I set up motion sensors.
ex.ja: モーションセンサーを取り付けたんだ。

note.ja: sense（感じる）+ -or。「感じとるもの」→「センサー」。

en: A prolonged military assault or a blockade of a city or fortress with the intent of conquering by force or attrition.
A period of struggle or difficulty, especially from illness.
To assault or blockade a city or fortress with the intent of conquering by force or attrition; to besiege.

siege.ety: From Middle English sege, from Old French sege, siege, seige (modern French siège), from Vulgar Latin *sēdicum, from Latin sēdicŭlum, sēdēcula (“small seat”), from Latin sēdēs (“seat”). The military sense of the term is derived from the notion of an army "sitting down" in front of its target.

ex.en: The castle was under siege for three months.
ex.ja: その城は３か月間包囲された。

note.ja: 古フランス語 sege（座ること）から。ラテン語 sedere（座る）。町の前に「座り込む」→「包囲」。sit と同じ sed。

en: The cardinal number occurring after fifty-nine and before sixty-one, represented in Roman numerals as LX and in Arabic numerals as 60.
A commercial lasting 60 seconds.

sixty.ety: Inherited from Middle English sixty, sexty, Old English sixtiġ, from Proto-Germanic *sehs tigiwiz (“sixty”), equivalent to six + -ty. Cognate with Scots sexty, saxty (“sixty”), Saterland Frisian säkstich (“sixty”), West Frisian sechstich (“sixty”), Dutch zestig (“sixty”), German Low German sesstig (“sixty”), German sechzig (“sixty”), Swedish sextio (“sixty”), Norwegian seksti (“sixty”), Icelandic sextíu (“sixty”). Compare also Sanskrit षष्टि (ṣaṣṭi).

ex.en: This machine can print sixty pages a minute.
ex.ja: この機械は１分間に６０ページ印刷できる。

ex.en: To tell the truth, he is still under sixty.
ex.ja: 実を言うと、彼はまだ６０歳になっていません。

ex.en: I should think she is over sixty.
ex.ja: 彼女は６０歳を過ぎていると思いますが。

note.ja: six + -ty（10）。

en: The part of a garment that covers the arm.
A (usually tubular) covering or lining to protect a piece of machinery etc.
To fit and attach a sleeve to an upper garment (e.g. to a shirt, blouse, sweater, jacket, coat, etc.) or to a folder.
To hide something up one's sleeve.

sleeve.ety:
From Middle English sleve, slefe, from Old English slīef and slīefe (“sleeve”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Sleeuwe (“sleeve”), West Frisian slúf, Dutch sloof (“apron”), Low German sluve, dialectal German Schlaube.

The head of a corporation's treasury department.

Not clearly or explicitly defined.

unclear.ety: From Middle English unclere, equivalent to un- + clear. Compare Saterland Frisian uunkloor (“unclear”), West Frisian ûnklear (“inoperative, broken”), Dutch onklaar (“out of order, defective, broken”), German unklar (“unclear”), Danish uklar (“unclear”), Swedish oklar (“unclear”).

ex.en: The meaning of this letter is unclear.
ex.ja: この手紙の意味は不明である。

note.ja: un（否定）+ clear（はっきりした）。「はっきりしない」。

en: Someone, usually male, who uses (or has skill with) magic, mystic items, and magical and mystical practices.
One who is especially skilled or unusually talented in a particular field.
To practice wizardry.
To conjure.

That has been taken in, engulfed, imbibed, or assimilated.

Litter and discarded refuse.

To be better than (something).

exceed.ety: From Middle English exceden, from Old French exceder, from Latin excēdō (“to go beyond”), from ex- (“out, forth”) with cēdō (“to go”); see cede and compare accede etc. Partly displaced native Old English ofersteppan, whence Modern English overstep.

ex.en: You were exceeding the speed limit, weren't you?
ex.ja: 制限速度を超えていましたね。

ex.en: Benefits of course should exceed the costs.
ex.ja: もちろん利潤は生産費を上回るべきです。

ex.en: The car is exceeding the speed limit.
ex.ja: その車は制限速度を超過している。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ ceed（進む）。限度の外へ進む →「超える・上回る」。excess（超過）。

en: To bar (someone or something) from entering; to keep out.
To expel; to put out.

exclude.ety: Borrowed from Latin exclūdō, from prefix ex- (“out”) + variant form of verb claudō (“close”).

ex.en: They decided to exclude him from their circle.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼を仲間からはずすことに決めた。

ex.en: All the members of our club, excluding me, are men.
ex.ja: うちのクラブはわたし以外、全員男です。

ex.en: He was excluded from the club.
ex.ja: 彼はクラブから除外された。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ clud（閉じる）+ e。外に閉め出す →「除外する・締め出す」。include（含む）と対。

en: Exceedingly violent, severe, ferocious, cruel or savage.
Resolute or strenuously active.

fierce.ety: From Middle English fers, fiers, borrowed from Old French fers (“wild", "ferocious”), nominative of fer, from Latin ferus (“wild", "untamed”).

ex.en: We are in a fierce competition with that company.
ex.ja: 我々はあの会社と激しく競争している。

ex.en: A fierce dog attacked the girl.
ex.ja: どう猛な犬が女の子に飛びかかった。

ex.en: A fierce battle was fought here.
ex.ja: ここで激戦が行われた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ferus（野生の）から。「野獣のような」→「どう猛な・激しい」。ferocious（凶暴な）も同じ。

en: A plant, Allium sativum, related to the onion, having a pungent bulb much used in cooking.
A preparation from Allium sativum used as a food ingredient or the flavor or other characteristics of such an ingredient.
To flavor with garlic.

garlic.ety: Inherited from Middle English garlek, garlik, from Old English gārlēac (“garlic”, literally “spear-leek”), from gār ("spear"; in reference to its sharp, tapering leaves) + lēac (“leek”). Cognate with Scots garlic (“garlic”), Faroese geirleykur (“garlic”), Icelandic geirlaukur (“garlic”).

ex.en: Garlic is used to improve the taste of food.
ex.ja: ニンニクは食べ物の味を良くするのに使われる。

ex.en: I don't like the smell of garlic.
ex.ja: ニンニクの臭いが嫌いなの。

ex.en: I hate the smell of garlic.
ex.ja: ニンニクの臭いが嫌いなの。

note.ja: 古英語 gārlēac ＝ gār（槍）+ lēac（ネギ）。「槍の形のネギ」→「ニンニク」。leek（西洋ネギ）。

en: The state of being grateful.

gratitude.ety:

From French gratitude, from Medieval Latin grātitūdō (“thankfulness”), from Latin grātus (“thankful”). Displaced Old English þancung.

ex.en: I have no words to express my gratitude.
ex.ja: 何ともお礼の言葉もございません。

ex.en: I would like to express my gratitude to her.
ex.ja: 私は彼女に感謝の気持ちを表したい。

ex.en: He showed no gratitude for the offer.
ex.ja: 彼はその申し出に感謝の気持ちを示さなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 gratus（ありがたい・喜ばしい）から。grateful、grace、congratulate と同じ grat。

en: Balls or pieces of ice falling as precipitation, often in connection with a thunderstorm.
An occurrence of this type of precipitation; a hailstorm.
To have hailstones fall from the sky.
To send or release hail.

hail.ety: From Middle English hayl, haul, from Old English hæġl, hæġel, hagol (“hail”), from Proto-West Germanic *hagl, from Proto-Germanic *haglaz, of uncertain origin. Either from Proto-Indo-European *kagʰlos (“pebble”); or alternatively from *ḱoḱló-, a reduplication of *ḱel- (“cold”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Hail (“hail”), West Frisian heil (“hail”), Low German Hagel (“hail”), German Hagel (“hail”), Dutch and Swedish hagel (“hail”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Icelandic hagl (“hail”). Compare also Old Norse héla (“frost”). Doublet of haglaz, if the second etymology (“cold”

ex.en: As a rule, hail falls in the summer.
ex.ja: 概してひょうは夏に降る。

ex.en: Have you ever seen it hail?
ex.ja: 雹が降るのを見たことがありますか。

ex.en: The crowd hailed the winner.
ex.ja: 群集は勝利者を歓呼して迎えた。

note.ja: 「あられ」は古英語 hægl から。「呼び止める・称賛する」は北欧語 heill（健康な）から、whole と同じ祖先で別語。
